title: Personal Credit Cards: Reversing Billed Fees
content:
A fee billed to Personal Credit Cards may be reversed on one of three grounds: the bank error ground, the courtesy waiver ground, or the final dispute ground. Whatever the ground, the reversal takes back the whole fee, never a part of it, as a single reversal entry linked to the fee concerned, and no fee can be reversed more than once.

## Bank error ground

A fee that this charter did not permit to be billed comes off on the bank error ground, and such reversals are unlimited. Illustrations of such fees include:

- a late fee where the minimum payment was in fact met on time under the rules for crediting payments;
- a late fee larger than the minimum payment that was missed;
- a late fee and a returned payment fee both billed for one missed payment;
- an annual fee billed although the first-year waiver, or the protection for service members on active duty, ruled it out.

## Courtesy waiver ground

The courtesy ground is available for a late payment fee and for no other fee. Every one of the following must hold on the bank's records at the time; if any of them fails, no courtesy reversal is granted:

| Requirement | How it is measured |
|---|---|
| Allowance not used up | the courtesy late fee reversals the customer received on all of their cards during the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the current date, that date included, number fewer than the tier's courtesy allowance |
| Good payment record | the statements immediately before the late one show at least the tier's required number of consecutive on-time payments |
| Account still open to service | the card account is active or suspended when the courtesy is granted |

A statement is paid on time when the payments and credits posted from its closing date through its due date reach its minimum payment. The run is counted statement by statement going backward, starting with the statement immediately before the late one, and it ends at the first statement that falls short.

## Final dispute ground

When a billing dispute ends in the cardholder's favour, fees that arose from the disputed charge are reversed on the final dispute ground.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

- Take an illustrative allowance of two courtesy reversals and an illustrative requirement of four on-time payments. A cardholder who received one courtesy reversal in the past 365 days, has five on-time statements before the late one and an active account meets every requirement: a count of one is below two.
- The same cardholder, had a second courtesy reversal been granted ten months ago on a different card, would have a count of two, which is not below the allowance of two; the courtesy ground is closed.
- A late fee billed although the payment was credited on the due date is taken back on the bank error ground, and no courtesy allowance is touched.
